label: sec:knot-centric-table-intro
html:
The conventional periodic table indexes each element by its atomic number Z and electron configuration, an ordering imposed from outside the object it catalogues. In the present framework an element is a knot: a nuclear Borromean shell structure dressed by electrons, the level words e_n = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_2\cdots\sigma_n of its occupied shells. Its most natural label is therefore intrinsic — the braid whose closure realizes that knot — and organizing the table knot-centrically replaces the external atomic-number bookkeeping with the element's own topological data.

Reading the table from its simplest cell makes the scheme concrete. Hydrogen occupies the first cell of the first row (the N = 0 harmonic-oscillator shell), where the nuclear side carries a single Borromean unit; heavier elements are built by adding shells to this seed. Each element is then indexed by its braid representative together with its Hecke level, and the grid arranges these indices so that rows track the nuclear harmonic-oscillator level N and columns track the proton sub-shell filling order.
